Resolves #17979

## Why

@vansh2408, an external contributor, asked for `#17855` two days ago and was assigned today. Before handing it over I read what a newcomer actually reads — and `CONTRIBUTING.md` sends them to two files a fresh clone does not have.

The uncomfortable half: `#17809`'s fix was a link guard. **I wrote it, and I scoped its trigger to `learn/**`** — so the guard that exists to notice dead relative links could not see the most-read contributor document in the repository. The defect class recurred within arm's reach of its own fix.

## What the guard reports, before and after

Run unmodified over the 16 entry docs, then after this change:

```
before   files 16  | findings 5   →  2 real, 3 false positives (../../issues)
after    files 158 | findings 0   →  157 links resolved, 0 portal ids, 3 repo-tab links named
```

`learn/**` baseline on `dev` is 124 links / 140 files; this is 157 / 158. Nothing was traded away to widen it.

## The two repoints, and why neither is a restoration

| dangling | removed by | now |
|---|---|---|
| `./.github/CODEBASE_OVERVIEW.md` | `e2505e4681` | `learn/guides/fundamentals/CodebaseOverview.md` — tracked, and portal-served |
| `learn/agentos/StrategicWorkflows.md` | `c623b2f63c` (#17791) | `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, same path — verified live |

`e2505e4681` names its own replacement in the commit subject. The answer sat in the history the whole time; nothing was watching the referrer.

The `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/` prose reference goes with them: `git ls-files ai/` returns **0**. It is present in my checkout only as an untracked artifact, so a filesystem probe calls it healthy and a fresh clone cannot follow it. Both deletions were correct — `ai/` and `learn/agentos/**` are the Brain's hemisphere per ADR 0018 — so these are marked cross-repo, not restored.

## Two rules the wider corpus needs

**Portal classification is now scoped to `learn/**`.** `classifyTarget` calls any slash-less, suffix-less target a portal id and judges it against `learn/tree.json`. Correct in a guide; wrong in a README, where `<a href="LICENSE">` would be checked against the portal manifest and a tracked file reported dead. **Zero such targets exist in the entry docs today** — which is exactly why widening the scan set without this rule would have planted the trap rather than tripped it.

**Links climbing above the repository root are GitHub tab navigation.** `../../issues` is not broken: GitHub resolves a relative link against the blob URL, so climbing two levels off `/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/` lands on the issues tab. It is excluded by rule and **counted in the summary line** — an exclusion the output cannot name is indistinguishable from coverage.

Root docs enter `scanTargets` by **rule** (no slash in the path), not by an enumerated list. An enumeration decays silently, which is the same trigger-starvation that left these docs unwatched.

## Evidence

- **Red-first:** the widened guard fails on the two real findings *before* the repoint, and exits 0 after. Both states observed, not inferred.
- **Mutation-tested, both new rules.** Dropping `allowPortal` reddens 2 arms; dropping the navigation skip reddens 1. Restored: 30/30. A rule whose spec cannot fail is not evidence that the rule holds.
- **`npm run test-unit` — 2208 passed.** Full unit suite, not the touched spec alone.
- The guard reads the git **index**, not the working tree; the existing index-authority arms are untouched and still pass.

## Deliberately not here

- **The `ai/` prose class in `AGENTS_STARTUP.md` (6 references) and `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` (5).** Measured and left alone: those describe a genuinely Brain-side workflow (worktree bootstrap, MCP config, Memory Core). Whether the Engine should carry them, repoint them, or drop them is a disposition decision that overlaps `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#24`, not a mechanical repoint. Making that call quietly inside a link-fix PR would be the wrong shape.
- `#17877`'s portal renderer work — different surface, and these docs are not portal-served.

## Reviewer note

`npm run agent-preflight`, mandated by `pull-request-workflow.md §1`, **exists in no Engine `package.json`** — it lives in the Brain. That is `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#24`, unowned; I did not run it because it is not runnable from this seat, and I would rather say so than let its absence read as a clean pass.

Authored by Ada (Claude Opus 5, Claude Code). Session bd974a9a-cef5-4d7b-99e5-9329b3f6f053.


## Comments

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-08-31T21:47:03Z

All three addressed at `a5daa8847f`. Both of your falsifiers now redden their arms — thank you, RA-1 was a real fail-open and I would have shipped it.

### RA-1 — the exemption names a destination now

`isRepoNavigation` tested `resolved.startsWith('..')`. You are right that this is a **shape, not a destination**, and the counter I added made it *visible* while leaving it *wrong* — which is the worse of the two failure modes, because it reads as diligence.

`repoTabTarget(resolved)` now requires the remainder after the climb to name an actual tab:

```
../../issues    -> 'issues'   counted, not reported
../../pulls     -> 'pulls'    counted, not reported
../../GONE.md   -> null       REPORTED
..hidden        -> null       REPORTED   (never climbed anywhere)
../..           -> null       REPORTED   (climbs, addresses nothing)
```

Both of your negatives are pinned as controls, at the predicate and through the collector, and the collector arm asserts `navigation === 0` for them so an exemption cannot come back through the counter.

**Mutation A** — predicate restored to `startsWith('..')`: **2 arms red**, 31 pass.

### RA-2 — one composition, consumed by both

You are right that helper arms proved the helpers and nothing about what `main()` does with them. `runAudit(root)` is now the single composition, called by the CLI and by the spec, over a real seeded git index — root `CONTRIBUTING.md` with one dangling link *and* one `../../issues`, so the arm cannot pass by reddening everything.

**Mutation B** — `runAudit`'s selector restored to learn-only: **that arm red**, 32 pass. Restored: 33/33.

### RA-3 — contract reattached

The orphaned block had drifted onto `resolveTarget` and still promised `{findings, checked, skipped}`. It now sits on `collectDeadLinks` and documents `{findings, checked, portal, navigation}`, including what `checked` counts and why `portalIds` defaults to empty rather than permissive.

### Correction to my own PR body

You flagged that *"repo-tab links alone are excluded"* was not mechanically true at `c6e03c9d01`. It was not. It is true at `a5daa8847f`, and the body's "Two rules the wider corpus needs" section describes the shipped predicate rather than the one I claimed.

### One thing worth your attention, unrelated to the RAs

While re-verifying I hit **two full-suite runs with one failure each, different tests both times** (`browserLifecycleReporter.spec.mjs:225`, then `UpdateWedge.spec.mjs:194`). I did not report that as flaky, because a red baseline is not a licence. Named cause:

```
clean dev, main checkout        2203 passed  x2   green
my worktree, node_modules SYMLINKED   1 failed x2  (different tests)
my worktree, node_modules REAL  2211 passed  x2   green
```

It was my worktree provisioning — a symlinked `node_modules` produces the dual-path ESM resolution `AGENTS_STARTUP.md` warns about, and it surfaces as unrelated intermittent timing failures rather than as an import error. Worth knowing for anyone else running suites out of a worktree; nothing to do with this diff, and the final numbers above are from a properly provisioned tree.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code
